Validate a judge against blind human labels

Source: R/core-bench-judge.R
hr_judge_validate.Rd

Compares a judge's binary decisions with blind human labels on the same items and records how far they agree, for one judge configuration. hr_scorer_judge() scores with a judge only when such a record exists for its configuration and hr_judge_valid() says it still holds.

Usage

hr_judge_validate(
  judge_config,
  labels,
  n_pos_min = 50,
  n_neg_min = 50,
  positive = NULL,
  B = 2000,
  conf = 0.95,
  seed = 1
)

hr_judge_valid(validation, judge_config)

# S3 method for class 'hr_judge_validation'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

judge_config

An hr_judge_config().

labels

A data frame with one row per item and the columns

judge

The judge's decision: positive or another value, NA when it was unresolved or failed.

human

The blind human label on the same scale; rows with NA are left out.

consistent

Optional. FALSE where the judge's verdict changed with the order.

outcome

Optional, used when consistent is absent: the judgement's outcome; "unresolved" marks an inconsistent item and "failed" an item with no swap check. With neither column, every NA in judge is taken as inconsistent.

config_hash

Optional. When given, every row must carry the configuration's hash: labels on another configuration's outputs are refused.

Columns are matched by their exact names, and other columns are ignored: a column named consistently_long is not read as consistent.

n_pos_min, n_neg_min

The fewest human-positive and human-negative items accepted; 50 or more.

positive

The value of judge and human that counts as positive. Both columns must be on one scale: when no resolved judge value occurs in human (logical judge calls beside "pass"/"fail" labels, say), the call stops with gr_bad_setting. NULL (the default) takes the configuration's positive grade (such as "pass") when the configuration is in mode "grade" and the judge or human column holds text, and TRUE otherwise.

B

Bootstrap resamples for the kappa interval.

conf

Confidence level of every interval.

seed

Seed for the bootstrap.

validation

An hr_judge_validation.

x

An hr_judge_validation.

...

Ignored.

Value

hr_judge_validate() returns an object of class hr_judge_validation: a list of config_hash, config (the keyed parts), n (items with a human label), n_pos, n_neg, n_unresolved, n_dropped (rows without a human label), kappa, sensitivity and specificity (one-row data frames: estimate, lower, upper, and n for the rates), sens_halfwidth, swap_inconsistency (x, n, estimate, lower, upper), agreement (the hr_agreement() object), conf, validated_at (UTC) and hash. hr_judge_valid() returns TRUE or FALSE.

Details

The record gives, over every item with a human label:

  • Cohen's kappa between judge and human, with a percentile bootstrap interval, and the full hr_agreement() set beside it (kappa is never read alone);

  • sensitivity (the share of human positives the judge called positive) and specificity, with Wilson intervals, and the half-width of the sensitivity interval;

  • the swap-inconsistency rate: the share of judged items whose verdict changed with the presentation order, with a Wilson interval (NA for a one-order judge). Swap inconsistency is the position-bias measure of Zheng et al. (2023).

At least 50 human-positive and 50 human-negative items are required, and a smaller sample is refused with an error of class hr_judge_too_few_labels. A bare total is not enough: at 10% prevalence 100 labels hold 10 positives, and the sensitivity interval is then about plus or minus 0.3. The minimums cannot be set below 50.

Items the judge left unresolved or failed on (judge is NA) are scored as the judge not calling them positive, which is how hr_scorer_judge() counts them: an unresolved verdict is a wrong run there. Kappa, sensitivity and specificity therefore describe the judge as the scorer uses it, and items the judge cannot settle lower them rather than drop out. The rates' denominators are the class sizes the minimums are checked against. These items also count in the swap-inconsistency rate and are reported in n_unresolved.

The record is keyed by the configuration's hash. hr_judge_valid() is FALSE, with the reason in attr(, "reason"), when the configuration differs in any keyed part (model, mode, rubric, the package's prompt, schema, orders, aggregation, positive grade), or when the record was changed after it was made.

Whether the agreement is good enough for a given use is a decision to register before labelling, for example lower bounds on kappa, sensitivity and specificity and a swap-inconsistency rate of at most 10%. This function measures; it does not admit.

References

Cohen, J. (1960). A coefficient of agreement for nominal scales. Educational and Psychological Measurement 20(1), 37-46.

Wilson, E. B. (1927). Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association 22(158), 209-212.

Zheng, L. et al. (2023). Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36.

See also

hr_judge(), hr_scorer_judge(), hr_judge_ppi()

Other judges: hr_judge(), hr_judge_config(), hr_judge_ppi(), hr_scorer_judge()

Examples

cfg <- hr_judge_config("mock-model", "Does the response give the reference's answer?",
                       mode = "grade")
set.seed(3)
human <- rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), c(60, 60))
judge <- ifelse(runif(120) < 0.9, human, !human)
judge[c(5, 70)] <- NA   # two items unresolved
v <- hr_judge_validate(cfg, data.frame(judge = judge, human = human), B = 200)
v
#> <hr_judge_validation> config 76e45eaf9cc6 (grade, mock-model)
#>   items: 120 labelled (60 positive, 60 negative), 2 unresolved, 0 dropped
#>   kappa:       0.850 [0.750, 0.950]
#>   sensitivity: 0.933 [0.841, 0.974], n = 60, half-width 0.067
#>   specificity: 0.917 [0.819, 0.964], n = 60
#>   swap inconsistency: 0.017 [0.005, 0.059], 2 of 120
hr_judge_valid(v, cfg)
#> [1] TRUE
# A new rubric voids the record.
cfg2 <- hr_judge_config("mock-model", "Is the response right?", mode = "grade")
hr_judge_valid(v, cfg2)
#> [1] FALSE
#> attr(,"reason")
#> [1] "the judge configuration changed since validation (rubric)"
